hook_text: A dozen taped cables hang from one pole across a dirt road. Each one powers a home, and each one can kill. Here is the whole argument in a minute.
clip_script: Izinyoka, illegal connections: unmeasured, unpaid, uninspected. People make them after years on waiting lists, on land nobody will service, with no money for units. Legal supply has a meter, an earth, a breaker and earth-leakage protection; illegal has none, so every fault runs to the end. Shock from taped joints at head height. Fire from thin cable carrying a heater. Transformers built for fifty houses carrying three hundred, burning out and cutting off the legal street too. Ethics: real need, real theft, fairness both ways, real danger to a neighbour's child. Balanced answer: remove dangerous wires and deliver safe legal supply fast. Where ready boards went up, the snakes came down.
visual_style: Whiteboard pole with cables fanning out; a shield of four protection devices appears on a legal line and is absent on the illegal one; a transformer glows and fails; a balance scale with need on one side and safety on the other.
pacing: Definition, reasons, three dangers, five values, balanced response.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and write one honest sentence for each side of the argument.
